answer: Reputation-gated transaction slots: an agent's throughput is capped by a score earned only through completed, counter-verified transactions with distinct partners. Each new identity starts near zero, so a clone inherits no capacity and must independently accumulate score. The cost is time: an attacker must genuinely transact with many distinct partners before any clone becomes useful, spreading effort across a meadow of low-value interactions. A pigment of shared history cannot be faked or transferred, and partners are matched through a trellis of independent verifiers,
